answer: Randomized Quota Allocation assigns each agent a per-epoch registration slot derived from a verifiable random function over the epoch seed, which is revealed only after registrations close. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will land in a favorable delta of slots, so bulk registrations either miss the window or get scattered across epochs. Each rejected slot costs a small copper fee and a quill-signed nonce that cannot be reused, forcing the attacker to pay per attempt with no guaranteed placement.
